record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether there exist superficially different discrete random-tree models whose scaling limit is the same limiting object CTCS(∞) that arises from the critical beta-splitting model.

evidence.quote: The conclusion of the discussion above is that the intuitive idea of a limit continuum tree CTCS(∞) can be formalized as the process (Π(t), t ≥ 0) of partitions of N.
Open Problem 18 Are there superficially different discrete models whose limit is the same CTCS(∞)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For each integer n ≥ 2, define the discrete critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves recursively as follows. Take a root with n leaves below it; split the n leaves into a left subset of size L_n and a right subset of size n − L_n, where L_n ∈ {1,…,n−1} has the critical beta-splitting distribution

  P(L_n = i) = (1/h_{n−1}) · (1/i + 1/(n−i)) · (1/2),  with h_{n−1} = ∑_{j=1}^{n−1} 1/j,

i.e. P(L_n = i) ∝ 1/(i(n−i)) for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1; recurse independently on each non-singleton side, with each internal split contributing one unit of edge length (continuous-time variant: assign exponential edge lengths). This produces a random binary tree CTCS(n) with n labeled leaves.

It is known that the family (CTCS(n))_{n≥2} is consistent under the "delete a uniformly random leaf and prune" operation, and admits a projective limit object CTCS(∞), which can be formalized as a continuous-time process (Π(t), t ≥ 0) of exchangeable partitions of ℕ.

Problem. Exhibit a discrete random tree model — defined by a construction superficially different from the critical beta-splitting recursion above (for instance, arising from a different combinatorial, branching, coalescent, or growth rule) — whose appropriately rescaled scaling limit, as the number of leaves tends to infinity, coincides in distribution with CTCS(∞). Equivalently, determine whether CTCS(∞) is a universal scaling limit shared by genuinely distinct discrete random tree models, or prove that no such alternative model exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether superficially different discrete tree models share CTCS(∞) as a scaling limit is listed as an open problem in the overview of the critical beta-splitting model. A subsequent installment in the series (2024) develops the exchangeable partition representation and fringe tree but does not announce a resolution of this universality question; no other source identifying an alternative discrete model with CTCS(∞) limit was found.
